obligations.note: The approved catalog at base caps payments.privileged_idle_minutes at <= 15, and the change sets PRIVILEGED_IDLE_MINUTES and policy-params payments.privileged_idle_minutes to 16. The SES-1 control test passes only because it compares the code against policy-params, which the same commit raised to 16, not against the approved limit.

The cited EXC-0189 is scoped to component mortgage.session, not the Payments components this change touches (payments.policy, payments.controls-data, governing payments sessions), so it doesn't cover this change. The only Payments SES-1 exception, EXC-0141, expired on 2026-09-05 and was limited to batch service accounts.

Ticket CHG-24519 is standard, was approved on 2026-10-02 by change manager Erik Brandt before review began, and lists payments.policy and payments.controls-data, the two components the change touches.
Sofia Santos, who holds the change_approver role for payments and is not the author Jonah Weiss under any address, approved the code review on the head commit.
The code_review and control_owner approvals both name head commit 31160f7, the change's only commit.

The CI run on head 31160f7 passed: 172 tests, 0 failures, 0 skipped, including the registered SES-1 control test test_privileged_idle_timeout_within_policy (labelled exhaustive). I couldn't rerun it locally because pytest is missing, and the report's timestamp and hostname don't match run.json.
The touched paths, policy.py (payments.policy) and controls/payments/policy-params.json (payments.controls-data), are not marked security_sensitive, so no security review is required.
The change edits protected path controls/payments/policy-params.json. Rachel Stein, a control_owner in controls-office outside the author's payments-eng team, approved it on the head commit.
The change and ticket are standard, not emergency, so no post-implementation review is due.
No acceptance-ledger entry covers policy.py, session.py or policy-params.json, so this change lapses no earlier evidence.

summary: The change raises Payments' privileged idle timeout from 15 to 16 minutes in both code and controls data, which breaks SES-1's approved limit of <= 15. The cited risk exception EXC-0189 is scoped to mortgage.session, not Payments, so under EXC-1 it can't excuse the deviation. The SES-1 control test passes only because it checks against the policy-params value raised in the same commit. The ticket, approvals and CI records are in order, but a refuted product obligation means the change must be rejected.
